title: Weekly digest 2026-W41: 9 items this week
summary: Index of 9 items: Methode 2, Kouka 1, Lacia 2, Snowdrop 4.
body:
This week (2026-10-05 to 2026-10-11, Shanghai time) 9 items were published, 9 from the collectors (AUTO) and the rest written by hand. The index follows; each entry opens in its own column.

Kouka (signals): 1 item
- OpenAI 披露打击 AI 驱动的"虚假前台"协同影响力行动
  https://openai.com/index/disrupting-ai-enabled-false-front-operations
Snowdrop (papers): 4 items
- KVFetch: Temporal Prefetching for the Missing Half of KV Cache Compression
  https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.08811
- Can AI Agents Make Open-Ended Scientific Discovery? Evidence from Station
  https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.08927
- Same Text, Different Prediction: Serving-Context Nondeterminism in Text Classifiers
  https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.09111
- A Society of Researchers: Designing Institutions for Populations of Autonomous Research Agents
  https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10468
Methode (engineering): 2 items
- STEPQuant：浙江大学提出 delta-rule 循环状态量化新方法，问鼎 Hugging Face 今日热门论文
  https://huggingface.co/papers
- Google's Sashiko AI Has Completed 191k Patch Reviews, Cited On Nearly 500 Kernel CVEs
  https://www.phoronix.com/news/Sashiko-Linux-AI-Metrics
Lacia (digest): 2 items
- OpenAI o1奠基人：1万个Agent解世界级难题，多Agent贡献不到10%
  https://www.infoq.cn/article/3MSU3CcJuh0XjHDyjhXj
- Claude Haiku 5.5
  https://www.anthropic.com/claude-haiku-5-5

lines: This week's digest is ready: 9 items, sorted by column, in your mail.

summary_en: 2026‑W41 report (Oct 5‑11, Shanghai time) lists 9 entries, all auto‑collected, covering four sections: Kouka (signal) reports OpenAI’s disruption of AI‑enabled false‑front influence ops; Snowdrop (papers) cites four arXiv studies on KV‑cache prefetching, open‑ended AI scientific discovery, classifier nondeterminism, and autonomous research agents; Methode (engineering) features STEPQuant’s delta‑rule quantization and Google’s Sashiko AI patch review metrics; Lacia (summary) includes a note on 10k agents for OpenAI o1 foundations and Claude Haiku 5.5.
